last_handoff.preorder_store_2026_08_22: THE ROUND: the founder opened paid pre-orders. Brainstormed to a locked set of decisions (money model, subdomain, Razorpay Standard Checkout, flow order, event QR pricing, Resend, policies, WhatsApp-only support number, no cap plus a dated deadline, balance by link, Supabase, four form fields, refunds by request, CTA label, test-keys-first rollout), then built in four commits: (1) the marketing site's promise, (2) the policy layer, (3) the store, (4) chrome separation. WHAT TO KNOW BEFORE TOUCHING IT: the client never sends a price (§8.25-c-i); paid is decided twice through one idempotent markPaid (§8.25-p); the webhook verifies the RAW body and releases its event claim on failure (§8.25-m); an address is authorised only by its signed token (§8.25-n); the finale is the ONLY outbound link to the store (§8.25-b); the store is noindex and its low SEO score is correct (§8.25-aa). THREE THINGS FOUND BY VERIFYING RATHER THAN REASONING: the store inherited the marketing navbar including a CTA pointing at a #reserve anchor it does not have; unmatched store URLs fell back to the root 404 in marketing chrome; and grepping HTML source reported a string that was only in the RSC payload. THE COPY GUARD EARNED ITS KEEP: test/preorder-copy.test.ts found three retired promises the manual sweep missed, one a hardcoded ship date the config change could not reach.

last_handoff.store_live_and_verified_2026_08_23: Built, merged, launched and verified in one session, then hardened after launch. THE THREE POST-LAUNCH FIXES ARE THE PART WORTH READING: none was caught by a green 622-test suite, and each came from looking at a real artefact. (1) The first real receipt greeted a customer as 'shweta' — found by reading the sent PDF. (2) A refunded order stayed in the dispatch queue, because the webhook only acted on payment events; the queue IS `where status='paid'`, so a cancelled customer would have been shipped a Lumi and invoiced ₹4,500, and the only safeguard was a human remembering to run an UPDATE. Found by re-reading the payment lifecycle after watching a real refund. A partial refund deliberately does NOT cancel, because the first refund issued was ₹489 of ₹499. (3) An orphaned payment had no recovery path even though our order_ref already travelled in the Razorpay order's receipt and notes. ALSO WORTH CARRYING: two process failures of mine are in the commits rather than smoothed over — a merge to production with a red suite, because the command printed the test summary instead of gating on it, and a rollback tag that first landed on the very merge it was meant to escape.
last_handoff.one_tap_and_cleanup_2026_08_23: THE ROUND: two founder changes to a live commercial site, plus the repo cleanup they asked for in the same breath. Change 1 inverted a law written the day before (§8.25-b) after checking that its REASON still gets served: the store page states price, ship date and refund promise above its own first field, read on a real 390px render, so removing the forced stop at the finale costs a parent nothing. Change 2 turned the age dropdown into a blank and, in doing so, surfaced that the email templates escaped no customer text — found by asking what free text implies rather than by a failing test. Change 3 deleted what was closed and moved what was merely old: the evidence for each deletion is named in current_phase, including three things deliberately kept. WHAT THIS ROUND TEACHES: a naive cleanup would have deleted the Lori/Lua/Robu renders and the mascot poses, because a plain grep finds neither (one is kept by a decision recorded only in a code comment, the other is loaded through a template string). Check how an asset is referenced before calling it dead. GATES: 770 tests in 90 files, tsc clean, build exit 0, qa:sweep 30/30 across 15 routes at 390 and 1280, and every marketing route re-counted in SERVED HTML (zero CTAs left pointing at the anchor, id='reserve' still present exactly once per page). ALSO THIS ROUND: FOUNDER-TODO.md was rewritten from 635 lines to 170 on the founder's request, completed items compressed to one or two lines each. It was not merely verbose, it was WRONG in four places: the ship date read 1 September in two of them, one whole section said 'no card payment has ever gone through this code' three sections below the one describing the real payment that proved everything, item 8 ended with a correction claiming GA4 is not wired, and the retired 500-unit cap and Tally form were restated as live. The file is now split into ⏳ OPEN and ✅ CLOSED; every pointer that named 'section 0' or a numbered item was repointed. LAST THING, AND IT IS A PROCESS NOTE: the test count was written into EIGHT documents and had drifted by one before the round ended, because the README front-door guard was added after the number was measured. The exact count now lives in this file's `tests.count` and nowhere else; every other document points here. Verify a claim before repeating it, and do not repeat a number that changes every round.
